overall: Atlanta ran significantly hotter than NWP models anticipated, with the day's high of 89.6°F recorded at 16:52 ET — roughly 4.5–6°F above what ECMWF, HRRR, and NBM had forecast. By 20:19 ET, the temperature has fallen to 84.2°F and is cooling at -1.8°F/hr with broken cloud cover (62%), confirming the diurnal peak has clearly passed. No convective activity materialized near the station today despite regional Flood Watches targeting areas south and southeast of Atlanta.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance was notably cold-biased today, with all three NWP solutions (ECMWF 83.3°F, HRRR 84.9°F, NBM 85.1°F) undershooting the observed peak by 4–6°F, likely due to underestimating afternoon mixing and cloud clearing. The INTRADAY model correctly locked onto the 88–89°F bucket (96.8% probability) once sufficient afternoon observations accumulated, while the META model spread probability across the 88–93°F range reflecting earlier uncertainty.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is effectively locked in at 89.6°F — the running maximum has been stationary since ~17:00 ET, the give-up classifier fired at hour 14.87 with 96% confidence, and the current cooling rate of -1.8°F/hr makes any new peak essentially impossible at this hour. Confidence is very high (>97%) that 89.6°F is the final TMAX for the day, placing it squarely in the 88–89°F bucket.
